title: But he has not tried the steep climb.
subtitle: The hard road that leads to salvation
then: Ibn Zayd said: {idea}will he not take the path which contains salvation and good?{/idea} The man who boasted of spending heaps never spent where it was hard. The surah now explains what the climb is.
now: You will pay for the expensive dinner without a second thought. Giving the same amount to a stranger in need feels like climbing a hill. {idea}That hill is the road.{/idea} The heaviness is a sign you have found it.
old: Good deeds should feel easy, or they are not for me.
new: The good that feels like a climb is often the one that saves me.
try: Do one good deed today that you have been avoiding because it feels hard.

title: And what will make you know the steep climb?
subtitle: A question that makes you lean in
then: The verse pauses to raise the question before the answer. Ibn Zayd: {idea}then He explains this path{/idea} with freeing a neck and giving food. The listener expects something grand. {idea}The answer is practical.{/idea}
now: You picture the great deed as moving abroad to dig wells or giving up everything. So you do nothing. {idea}The next verses name things you can do this week.{/idea}
old: The deeds that really count are beyond someone like me.
new: The steep climb is made of real, nearby acts I can start.
try: Read verses 13-16 and pick the one you could do soonest.

title: Freeing a neck from bondage.
subtitle: The first step of the climb: setting someone free

row.title: you freed
sub: limb for limb from the Fire

key.label: What it did to the giver

then: The Prophet ﷺ said: {reward}whoever frees a believing slave, Allah will free for every limb of it a limb of his from the Fire.{/reward} When Ali ibn Al-Husayn heard this, he called his swiftest servant and said: {reward}go, you are free for the Face of Allah.{/reward}
now: Someone near you is trapped: a friend buried in debt, a relative who cannot pay a fine, a worker stuck without papers or pay. {idea}Helping lift a weight off someone's neck is part of this climb.{/idea}
old: Freeing slaves is from a world that no longer exists.
new: Lifting someone out of what traps them is still the steep climb.
try: Help someone with one burden they cannot lift alone: a bill, a form, a debt.

title: Or giving food on a day of hunger.
subtitle: Feeding when food is scarce and precious
then: Ibn Abbas said masghabah means {trap}hunger{/trap}, and Ikrimah, Mujahid and Qatadah agreed. Feeding on an ordinary day is good. {idea}Feeding on a day when everyone is hungry is the climb{/idea}, because you need the food too.
now: Prices went up. The shopping basket costs double. It is exactly the month you feel you cannot give. {idea}That is the day of hunger the verse means.{/idea} A small share then weighs more.
old: I will give when I have more spare money.
new: Giving in a tight season is the steep part, and it counts the most.
try: Buy or cook one extra meal this week and give it to someone who needs it.

title: To an orphan who is your own relative.
subtitle: Charity to family counts twice
then: Ibn Abbas, Ikrimah and others said: {idea}an orphan who is related to him.{/idea} The Prophet ﷺ said {reward}charity to a poor person is one charity, and to a relative it is two: charity and keeping ties.{/reward}
now: A cousin's child whose father died. A niece being raised by one parent on a low wage. They are not on a charity poster. {idea}They are in your family WhatsApp.{/idea}
old: Charity is for strangers in poor countries.
new: The orphan in my own family may be my first and double charity.
try: Think of a child in your extended family who lost a parent, and do one thing for them this week.

title: Or a poor person lying in the dust.
subtitle: The destitute with nothing between them and the dirt
then: Ibn Kathir: {trap}poor, miserable, and clinging to the dirt{/trap}, those in destitution. Ibn Abbas said: {trap}the one lying in the street with no house or anything to protect him against the dirt.{/trap}
now: The person in a sleeping bag outside the station. You walk past every morning with your coffee. {idea}The verse calls feeding them part of the climb that saves you.{/idea}
old: The homeless person on my street is not my responsibility.
new: The person in the dust is part of the steep path Allah showed me.
try: Buy a hot drink or meal for someone living on the street, and greet them by asking their name.

title: Then be among believers who urge patience and mercy.
subtitle: Faith, and a circle that encourages patience and compassion
then: Ibn Kathir: with these deeds {idea}he was a believer in his heart, seeking reward from Allah.{/idea} They advised each other {idea}to be patient with the harms of people, and merciful with them.{/idea} The hadith: {reward}be merciful to those on earth, and the One above will be merciful to you.{/reward}
now: Your friend vents about her difficult mother-in-law. You can add fuel, or say: be patient, be kind, Allah sees it. {idea}The verse wants you to be the second kind of friend{/idea}, and to have friends like that too.
old: Good deeds are my private business. My friends do not matter.
new: I need people who push me to patience and mercy, and I can be one.
try: Encourage one friend today to be patient or gentle in something they are facing.

title: Those are the people of the right.
subtitle: Where the steep climb ends
then: Ibn Kathir: {reward}those who have these characteristics are the companions of the right hand.{/reward} The man who boasted of spending heaps is answered here: {idea}the same wealth, spent on the climb, would have put him on the right.{/idea}
now: Same salary, two possible stories. One goes on things that impress people. The other quietly pays for a stranger's groceries and a cousin's school fees. {reward}Only one ends on the right.{/reward}
old: Where I end up depends on how much I have.
new: Where I end up depends on how I spend what I have.
try: Redirect one planned 'show' purchase this month toward someone in need.

title: Those who rejected Our signs are the people of the left.
subtitle: The other road, chosen by rejecting the signs
then: Ibn Kathir: {trap}the companions of the left hand.{/trap} The surah showed two roads in verse 10. Here they end. The difference is not wealth or strength, but {idea}whether a person accepted Allah's signs.{/idea}
now: Signs are everywhere in this surah: your eyes, your lips, the city you face in prayer. {idea}The question for you is not about other people.{/idea} It is which of these signs you are ignoring today.
old: The people of the left are people very unlike me.
new: The left is the end of ignoring signs. I check where I am ignoring them.
try: Pick one sign from this surah, your eyes or your tongue, and thank Allah for it out loud.

title: Over them a Fire closed in.
subtitle: A door that will be shut, so walk through mercy now

picture.label: The end of the left road

then: Many of the early scholars said mu'sadah means {trap}shut.{/trap} Ibn Abbas said: {trap}its doors will be closed.{/trap} The surah ends soberly, after laying out in detail {idea}the open road of freeing, feeding and mercy.{/idea}
now: Today every door is still open: the food bank, the orphan in your family, the friend who needs patience. {reward}The surah ends with a closed door so you hurry through the open ones.{/reward}
old: There will always be time to do good later.
new: Doors open today will not always be open. I walk through one now.
try: Do one of the deeds from verses 13-17 before the end of tomorrow.
